explain.say: Pilots use a checklist before every flight, so nothing is missed. You can use one for your writing too! Look at the checklist on the board. Here is our sentence: the cat sat on a mat.

faq.a: A capital letter is the big version of a letter, like T instead of t. Sentences and names start with one.

faq.q: Where does a full stop go?
faq.a: At the very end of a sentence, sitting on the line right after the last word.

faq.q: Why read my writing out loud?
faq.a: Your ears catch things your eyes miss, like a missing word. If it sounds right, it probably makes sense.

faq.q: Do I check everything at once?
faq.a: No, check one thing at a time. Look only for capitals first, then only for full stops, and so on.
asks: How do I use a checklist?

faq.q: What if I find lots of mistakes?
faq.a: That means your checking works! Fix them one at a time. A teacher or grown-up can check with you.

facts: In English, a sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark.
Pilots use checklists before flights so that no step is missed.

quiz.say: What should the start of a sentence have?
quiz.why: Every sentence starts with a capital letter.

wrong.1: A full stop goes at the end, not the start.
wrong.2: Sentences start with a capital letter, not a number.

quiz.say: How many words are in: The cat sat on a mat?
quiz.show: How many words: The cat sat on a mat?
quiz.why: The, cat, sat, on, a, mat: six words.

wrong.0: Count again: there are six words.
wrong.2: There are six words, not seven.
